routes.description: Establish that religious faith is an unnecessary and unreliable inference from human experience, that moral judgment and meaning remain available without divine authority, and that supernatural authorization can magnify coercion, textual injustice, and conflict.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if it connects a reason-based naturalistic account of existence and experience to a nonreligious basis for ethical judgment and human meaning, while showing why faith's claims to revelation, authority, consolation, and moral benefit do not overcome its epistemic and practical liabilities.

motionBridge.description: Show that reasoned naturalistic inquiry, autonomous moral judgment, and honest engagement with mortality better satisfy the motion's explanatory and ethical demands than religious projection, authority, or consolation.

centralBridges.description: Account for cosmic and biological reality through testable natural processes and explain why neither mystery nor a possible first cause establishes a supervising religious deity.
Establish that uncertainty and transcendent experience call for inquiry and proportioned belief rather than revelation, inherited faith, or appeals to the private beliefs of scientific authorities.
Explain how shared human capacities and contextual ethical reasoning can ground moral conduct without divine command, and why secular institutions may be needed to constrain religious authority.
Connect authoritative texts and supernatural mandates to coercion, exclusion, proselytism, or intensified conflict without requiring the claim that religion causes every human wrong.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that awe, love, beauty, grief, and numinous experience can retain significance without supporting a supernatural inference.
Defend candid acceptance of mortality and suffering as a viable source of dignity and reflection without promises of divinely guaranteed consolation.

routes.description: Establish that reality, agency, objective morality, sacred experience, and enduring meaning rationally support a transcendent divine source, while showing that an evolving Jewish tradition can guide ethical life without being reduced to ancient defects or every harm committed in religion's name.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if it gives a coherent positive basis for relating existence, consciousness, freedom, and binding goodness to God; identifies distinctive motivational, communal, and existential functions of faith; and answers projection, textual-harm, and religious-violence objections without treating faith as a scientific hypothesis.

motionBridge.description: Show that religious faith can disclose a transcendent source of existence, binding moral meaning, and human freedom while sustaining purposeful relationship and communal life.

centralBridges.description: Explain why existence, consciousness, love, and meaning can rationally indicate a reality beyond matter and support relationship with a transcendent God.
Connect genuine human choice and universally binding moral obligation to an immaterial or divine dimension while preserving a role for ethical reasoning.
Establish that sacred practice and religious community can motivate service, deepen intimate meaning, and provide substantial orientation amid death and bereavement.
Show how a historically transmitted and interpretive religious tradition can refine inherited defects and direct adherents toward justice without making every ancient rule permanently controlling.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish psychological explanations for why people believe from arguments about whether the content of religious belief is true.
Separate religion's claimed ethical purpose from violence rooted in land, power, resources, and ordinary aggression, while accounting for harms committed under religious identities.

sections.title: Divine Reality, Natural Explanation, and Epistemic Warrant
sections.rationale: This section encompasses the debate’s foundational clash over whether existence, consciousness, transcendent experience, and cosmic mystery warrant belief in God or are better approached through natural explanation, skepticism, and proportioned inquiry.

sections.title: Human Freedom and the Ground of Moral Obligation
sections.rationale: This section addresses whether genuine agency and universally binding moral duties require an immaterial divine ground or can arise through contingent natural processes, shared human capacities, and contextual ethical judgment.

sections.title: Sacred Meaning, Human Experience, and Mortality
sections.rationale: This section covers whether faith uniquely discloses sanctity, love, purpose, and sustaining consolation amid death and grief, or whether those experiences retain dignity and significance without supernatural promises.

sections.title: Religious Tradition, Practice, and Moral Authority
sections.rationale: This section examines whether evolving scripture, interpretation, community, and service refine moral life and motivate distinctive goods, or whether autonomous judgment and secular institutions are necessary to test and constrain religious authority.

sections.title: Projection, Supernatural Authority, and Religious Harm
sections.rationale: This section captures the dispute over whether religion projects human needs into coercive authority and amplifies textual injustice, proselytism, tribal conflict, and theocracy, or whether such harms chiefly reflect ordinary human aggression rather than faith’s ethical purpose.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: God is a human, fear-driven projection offering paternal consolation and substituting commanding celestial authority for independent moral thought.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Modern cosmology and evolution offer verifiable and awe-inspiring natural accounts, while extinction, waste, and contingency count against purposeful religious creation.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Random mutation, natural selection, and contingent evolutionary branching undermine the claim that material natural history must be wholly predetermined.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Because expanding scientific knowledge also enlarges awareness of the unknown, mystery calls for skepticism, inquiry, debate, and doubt rather than faith.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: Biblical moral commands coexist with divinely enjoined persecution, slavery, misogyny, and primitive property relations, making the authoritative text itself subject to moral criticism.

chunk-002:c002-07.proposition: Honest acceptance of mortality, entropy, grief, and struggle can foster stoicism and reflection without religious promises of eternal consolation.

chunk-002:c002-10.proposition: Religion can intensify ordinary tribal aggression by supplying divine mandates that magnify conquest, territorial disputes, genocide, and political violence.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-03.proposition: The broadly shared Golden Rule is a human ethical approximation whose necessary qualifications demonstrate that morality requires contextual judgment rather than absolute obedience.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-06.proposition: Human beings genuinely experience transcendence, ecstasy, beauty, love, and melancholy through nature and mortal life without those experiences revealing a supernatural dimension.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-09.proposition: Religious institutions cannot claim exclusive moral authority when secular law and constitutional government must restrain institutional abuse and discipline religious doctrine.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: God is the source of everything that exists and a transcendent reality with whom humans can have a relationship and align their lives, despite limits on human comprehension.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Attributing religious belief to fear, weakness, or psychological need does not disprove its content, because a believer's motive and the truth of the belief are separate questions.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: The reality and influence of consciousness, ideas, love, meaning, and existence itself support regarding the intangible as real and make a divine source intellectually plausible.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Because people do not choose their genetics, birth, or environment, genuine free choice requires an immaterial aspect of persons rather than determination by those material conditions alone.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: Jewish scripture and interpretation repeatedly command love of neighbor, pursuit of justice, and refinement of character, giving the tradition substantive resources for moral development.

chunk-002:c002-04.proposition: A religious tradition transmitted through history can acknowledge human composition and gradually refine inherited moral defects rather than treating every ancient provision as permanently controlling.

chunk-002:c002-06.proposition: Religious belief can motivate conduct that people might not otherwise undertake and can make intimate practices, such as a parent's blessing, experiences of sanctity rather than ordinary affection alone.

chunk-002:c002-08.proposition: Communal prayer and belief that the world is meaningful can provide profound comfort to dying and bereaved people when they confront severe anguish and loss.

chunk-002:c002-09.proposition: Most conflicts involving religious groups arise from land, power, resources, and ordinary human aggression, and the persistence of violence without religion indicates that faith is not its sole underlying cause.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-04.proposition: Jewish tradition preserves questioning and ethical reasoning while holding that a divine dimension grounds real right and wrong beyond evolved preference, comparative advantage, or power.
